newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower with others on Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower with others on Greenspan.

text.p: Italian shares ended lower with other stock markets on Wednesday, extending losses as U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan warned the U.S. stock market's rise may be "unsustainable" before the market edged back a touch in late trade.
Wall Street fell more than 100 points after Greenspan gave his warning over skyrocketing stock prices but pared some of the losses after what traders said was a kneejerk reaction.
In Milan, the March FIB30 futures contract dropped below a key level of 18,000 to 17,925 before recovering some ground.
The All-share Mibtel index ended 1.96 pct down at 12,083 after low of 12,031 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed off 2.13 pct at 17,988.
"There was selling across the board," one trader said. "If the bourse indices fall below current levels there'll be room for a considerable correction."

Banks were under pressure, with Banca Commerciale Italiana down 4.66 percent to 3,500 lire and Banca di Roma off 4.05 percent to 1,278. San Paolo, after two sessions of gains on good 1996 results, lost 1.56 percent to 12,000.

Telecoms also fared poorly. Telecom Italia, the most traded stock with nearly 15 million shares changing hands, fell 3.54 percent to 4,200 lire. Stet holding lost 3.27 percent to 7,760 and mobile phone operator TIM slipped 0.93 percent to 4,680.

Energy group ENI lost 1.49 percent to 8,700 lire, Fiat shed 1.26 percent to 5,245 and Olivetti slipped 0.88 percent to 622. Olivetti earlier denied Italian press reports of a slight delay in the sale of its PC business to Piedmont International.
Motorway caterer Autogrill was one of the few stocks to bucked the trend, closing 2.27 percent firmer at 2,250 lire.
